newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Mexico, Chile back rights post for Irish president.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, Chile back rights post for Irish president.

text.p: Mexico and Chile said on Monday they would back a bid by Irish President Mary Robinson to be appointed the next United Nations Commissioner for Human Rights.
"She is an oustanding person and we would be very happy to support her candidacy," Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria told reporters after a meeting with his European Union counterparts.
EU diplomats said Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza told his Irish counterpart Dick Spring that he too would back Robinson's campaign.
Diplomats said Spring had been canvassing support for Robinson on the fringes of a two-day meeting between the 15-member EU and 11 Latin American nations which began on Monday.
Robinson's main rival for the job -- apart from timing -- appears to be Sonia Picado, currently Costa Rica's ambassador to the United States.
Robinson is due to stand down as Irish President at the end of this year and it is unclear if she would quit early if offered the U.N. job.
The post became vacant last month when Jose Ayala Lasso resigned to become Ecuador's foreign minister and many Latin American countires were expected to support another candidate from that continent.

Robinson -- who is believed also to command considerable support from many African nations -- may run into opposition from Asian countries following Ireland's decision to back a Danish U.N. resolution criticizing China's human rights record.
Lasso was appointed the first commissioner to head the Geneva-based body in 1994 for a four-year term.
